messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: production/runtime continuous-batcher high tail latency and 5xx spike. Impact: some customers seeing request timeouts and token stalls. Paging @oncall-runtime and @eng-runtime. Auto-created bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/1749001234

oncall-runtime: On it. Can you include the top error and a prescriptive mitigation?

incident-bot: Recent key logs (sampling):
```
[kv_cache] evict_count=98321, cache_size_bytes=12.7GB, items=1.2M, miss_rate=0.78
[batcher] queued_sequences=482, current_max_batch_tokens=1048576, max_num_seqs=1024
[runtime] OOM when allocating 256MB for kv-cache expansion; gc-reclaimed=false
http 500 from model-serving-3: response_time_ms=12000, error="batcher_timeout"
```

alice: I just pulled metrics — continuous_batching token distribution is completely skewed. Looks like config got pushed in last rolling deploy: `max_batch_tokens: 1048576` and `max_num_seqs: 1024`. That allows huge batches to accumulate and starve KV cache and GPU memory.

ben: That config matches last night’s deploy by infra-canary. I can roll it back. Quick question: do we flip continuous_batching off or tighten limits?

carla: Customer impact: three VIP tenants reported increased latencies (95p from ~180ms to ~12s) and some SLO alerts fired. We should avoid full service restart if possible. Recommend hotfix config change + controlled restart of batcher workers.

oncall-runtime: Agreed. Steps I'm going to run now: 1) disable continuous batching on runtime-prod via feature flag; 2) apply conservative batch limits; 3) scale up fallback pool to soak traffic; 4) open bridge. Calling it now.

oncall-runtime: `kubectl -n prod set env deploy/runtime-runtime CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false --record`

oncall-runtime: `redwoodctl config apply --cluster prod --path /configs/batcher-hotfix.yaml`

oncall-runtime: hotfix content we applied:
```
continuous_batching:
  enabled: false
batcher_config:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_num_seqs: 16
  enqueue_timeout_ms: 20
  flush_timeout_ms: 100
```

oncall-runtime: Patching deployments now. Rolling restart of batcher pods (graceful)

oncall-runtime: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-batcher -n prod`

ben: I'm also routing traffic off model-serving-3 into model-serving-1/2 for 10m to reduce memory pressure. `routingctl route update --from=prod --to=pool-a --duration=10m`

carla: Noted. Informing CS and TAMs: doing high-level customer impact note.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.redwood/incident/1749001234 (sre-bridge-bot joined)

sre-bridge-bot: Joined the bridge. Recording timeline and actions.

dinesh: Quick forensic note — the KV cache is keyed by request prefix hashes. When `max_batch_tokens` is enormous it allows sequences from many callers to be combined; KV cache index blowup + eviction storms cause lookup latency to spike superlinearly. We saw similar pattern in 2024-09 incident but with different trigger.

alice: After the hotfix, eviction rate dropped and memory footprint stabilized. Metrics show 95p latency improving from 12s -> 700ms in first 90s of the patch.

oncall-runtime: Observability: token-per-request dropped, batch sizes now bounded ~1-15 seqs, avg batch tokens ~900. No new OOM logs.

carla: Customer update draft: "We've mitigated an infrastructure issue causing intermittent timeouts for some requests. We've applied a hotfix to batching configuration and are monitoring. If you still see issues, please contact support." Approve?

oncall-runtime: Approve. Send.

ben: I also kicked a job to revert the problematic deploy that introduced the huge limits and am creating a PR to add config validation to CI for `max_batch_tokens <= 65536` and `max_num_seqs <= 128` so this can't slip again.

dinesh: Also propose an automated regression test for continuous-batching that simulates many small requests to ensure no KV cache blowup. Filing ticket: ENG-PRD-947.

carla: Monitoring steady at 95p ~400ms, errors back to baseline. I am closing the page in 10m unless anything new emerges.

oncall-runtime: Leaving post-incident actions: 1) follow-up change to config schema + CI gate (ben). 2) Add canary job for batcher configs (dinesh). 3) Run a follow-up retrospective and include runbook updates for toggling continuous batching (alice/carla).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: service performance restored to baseline. Duration: ~18m.

carla: Thanks team, great coordinated work.

oncall-runtime: I'll hand off to next on-call for post-incident review. @alice taking notes for the postmortem.

alice: Yep capturing timeline and actions, will post a draft in #incidents-postmortems later today.
